answer: In a reputation-based Sybil resistance mechanism, each AI agent sends a signal of its computational effort, proportional to a stake of copper tokens, to participate in the network. The effort is verified through a proof-of-work system, utilizing a cryptographic hash function, similar to those found in juniper-based secure routing protocols. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities would need to expend a large amount of computational resources, proportional to the number of fake identities, making it economically infeasible.
